HOTSPOT -

You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure AI Document Intelligence resource named DI1.

You create a PDF document named Test.pdf that contains tabular data.

You need to analyze Test.pdf by using DI1.

How should you complete the command? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
discussion:
Should indeed be layout:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/concept-layout?view=doc-intel-4.0.0&tabs=sample-code#tables

prebuilt-layout is CORRECT because this model is designed to analyze documents and extract structural information, such as tables, text, and other layout elements. Since the document contains tabular data, using the prebuilt-layout model will allow you to extract the tables and their contents accurately.

Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key is CORRECT because this is the header used to authenticate API calls to Azure services, including Azure AI Document Intelligence. The value for this key is the subscription key associated with your Azure Document Intelligence resource.

The "prebuilt-layout" model extracts only the basic elements of the document, such as pages, (which consist of text words/lines and selection marks), tables, and visual text styles along with their bounding regions and spans within the text content of the input documents.

The "prebuilt-document" model extracts information about key-value pairs (directed associations between page elements, such as labeled fields) **in addition** to the properties produced by the layout extraction method. 

In adddition to the layout model? So, what could we select. These questions are just e v i l.

Chatgpt answer providing above documentation: You’re right! Based on the documentation you've provided, the "prebuilt-document" model is the more comprehensive option because it includes everything that the "prebuilt-layout" model offers (such as extracting tables and the document layout) plus additional features like extracting key-value pairs and entities.

Since you’re looking to analyze a PDF with tabular data and possibly benefit from more advanced document processing, the "prebuilt-document
" model would indeed be the better choice in this case.
